The video opens with a screen showing a music production program interface, displaying multiple tracks with audio waveforms. Superimposed in bold white text with a black outline is the phrase "SKRILLEX VOCAL CHOP CHORDS." This title implies the video will be a tutorial on how to create Skrillex-style vocal chops and chords. After a brief musical segment with vocal chops, the video transitions to a shot of a person, presumably the tutorial creator. He is wearing round glasses and a black hoodie with "ODYSSEY" written across it in pink and blue. He speaks directly to the camera, using hand gestures for emphasis. Then, there is a screen-shot that shows the Serum VST plugin. He continues to talk about how good the plugin is, then, another screen-shot appears which shows the Serum plugin website and information: "Xfer Records. Serum. RENT-TO-OWN. $9.99/mo. for 19 months." Finally, the video returns to the person again, emphasizing that the video is "**not even sponsored**" and uses a hand gesture to imply, "call me." The background includes a keyboard, microphone, and a white shelving unit with some storage boxes, giving the impression of a home studio setup.

The video opens with a shot of a man with tan skin, black hair pulled back into a bun, and round glasses. He is sitting in front of a keyboard and wearing a black hoodie with the word "ODYSSEY" emblazoned on it. He is waving his hand toward the camera with a cheerful expression. The background reveals a kitchen setting with wooden cabinets, a microwave, and various utensils. The screen then transitions to a vibrant gradient background of purples and pinks, showcasing the text "FB2B" in white, outlined with a thin line, seemingly a logo. Next, the scene cuts back to the man in his hoodie, now seated in front of a computer screen displaying a music production software, Ableton. The screen captures an array of audio clips and waveforms, with text overlays emphasizing "1. Find Acapella." A caption further clarifies that while he usually uses his own vocals, for demonstration purposes, he is using an acapella from a sample pack. In the lower portion of the video, we can see that the acapella is playing the words "You and I" in a high pitch.
